headline: Aid, Agents and the Data Plumbing
thesis: A new report finds 960,000 students lost federal aid over academic-progress rules, as AI agents widen the security perimeter and standards bodies gather to wire up learn-to-work data.
summary: Wednesday's digest leads with student aid and federal pressure. A Lumina Foundation and Mathematica report covered by Inside Higher Ed finds roughly 960,000 students lost federal aid in 2025 after failing satisfactory-academic-progress checks, and argues most colleges are not using the flexibility the law allows; meanwhile seven college presidents told journalists their priorities are stabilizing research funding and easing international-enrollment limits, days after a federal judge vacated the administration's student-visa duration rule. On the K-12 side, an EdSurge study of teachers using chatbots shows why teacher judgment still matters when AI suggests Minecraft for a lesson on circles. Security remains a drumbeat: THE Journal tracks a 41% surge in spear-phishing, an 84% rate of AI-related incidents and new just-in-time access controls for AI agents, and hosts an education e-mail security webcast today. On the data front, 1EdTech's Member Assembly opens today in North Charleston and Ed-Fi points to statewide attendance dashboards in South Carolina, while EDUCAUSE's annual conference begins in Orlando.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 18, 2026 · Items were gathered via web search (direct site fetches were unavailable); ISTE, Brookings, EdTech Week and Education Technology Insights had no new dated items, so evergreen pieces are shown. Some event dates come from source listings and should be confirmed.
